name: Crypto trend (BTC and ETH above 100-day average, long only)
sources: Liu, Y. and Tsyvinski, A., "Risks and Returns of Cryptocurrency", Review of Financial Studies 34(6), 2021, 2689-2727 (NBER working paper w24877), DOI https://doi.org/10.1093/rfs/hhaa113. CHECKED against the actual paper text on 2026-09-23 (WP8.2-style, by hand): real paper, confirmed. Confirmed 'documented only IN SPIRIT' is accurate, not a stretch: the paper documents time-series momentum as a general return-predictability factor via return-quintile sorts (Tables 14/15/17), with no mention anywhere of a moving-average or a 100-day rule specifically -- 'moving average' appears exactly once in the whole paper, unrelated (a macro control variable's own definition, not a trading rule). The specific 100-day-SMA rule is genuinely this entry's own construction, not the paper's. On 2026-10-17 the bibliographic record (authors, journal, volume 34 issue 6, pages 2689-2727) and the published abstract were also checked against Crossref (DOI 10.1093/rfs/hhaa113); the abstract states 'there is a strong time-series momentum effect' for cryptocurrency returns. That is the only thing claimed from this source: no Sharpe figure, return figure or sample window from the paper is claimed here.

Liu, Y., Tsyvinski, A. and Wu, X., "Common Risk Factors in Cryptocurrency", Journal of Finance 77(2), 2022, 1133-1177, DOI https://doi.org/10.1111/jofi.13119. Bibliographic record and abstract checked against Crossref on 2026-10-17 (abstract level only; the full text was not read for this entry). The abstract names momentum as one of three factors (cryptocurrency market, size, and momentum) that capture CROSS-SECTIONAL expected cryptocurrency returns. That is a cross-sectional momentum result, not a time-series (own-price, moving-average) trend result, so it is cited as adjacent literature on crypto momentum only and does NOT document this entry's rule.

Hurst, B., Ooi, Y. H. and Pedersen, L. H., "A Century of Evidence on Trend-Following Investing", Journal of Portfolio Management 44(1), 2017, 15-29, DOI https://doi.org/10.3905/jpm.2017.44.1.015. Bibliographic record checked against Crossref on 2026-10-17; Crossref returns no abstract for it and the paper text was not read for this entry, so NO claim from it is recorded in citation_claims. Cited as the general multi-asset trend-following reference (traditional asset classes, not cryptocurrency); it is not evidence about crypto.

Reference implementation: weightsim_rules::ladder rule id "crypto_trend_100d" (S3), the compiled rule replication::registry::certified_key_bars resolves against the embedded, SHA-256-pinned replication_ladder_crypto_evidence answer key (Amendment 13, crypto_evidence_v1, PR #213).

quotes: there is a strong time-series momentum effect

rule_text: Universe: BTC/USD and ETH/USD (daily closes). Each day, for each coin: if its close is above the simple average of its last 100 daily closes, INCLUDING today's close, hold that coin long at 50% of the sleeve's equity; otherwise hold cash in its place. Rebalance daily at the close. A position decided at the close of day t earns returns from the next trading day's close-to-close return onward; a decision uses only data available at the close of the decision day. Long only, no leverage: maximum gross exposure is 100% of sleeve equity (2 x 50%).
reference_implementation: weightsim_rules::ladder rule id "crypto_trend_100d" (S3), the compiled rule replication::registry::certified_key_bars resolves against the embedded, SHA-256-pinned replication_ladder_crypto_evidence answer key.

notes: min_history_years is the history needed to compute the FIRST signal only (100 daily closes); a meaningful backtest needs far more.

Drafted from RuleTemplate::CryptoTrend100d (library_curation::draft) -- structural fields (requirements, rebalance, parameters, rule_text) are template-fixed, matched here exactly to avoid RULE_DRIFT against the compiled rule.

The published rule rebalances daily to fixed 50/50 weights. The platform runs each coin as an independent sub-account, so weights drift: an approximation of the rule, not a block (cross_asset_rebalance = preferred).

rebalance.detail: Daily at the close of the (UTC) daily bar. Crypto trades every day, so no month-end or holiday handling is needed.

expected_ranges.source: No band, deliberately. Council rulings R22/R23 (COUNCIL_DATA_GATE_2026_09_26.md) and Amendment 13 section 7 (program/tests/fixtures/replication_ladder_crypto_evidence/AMENDMENT_13.md): expected ranges come from the certified window only, and with an estimated SE of about 0.49 on a single ~6.5-year window (one crypto cycle, not several independent ones), the band stays withdrawn until net-of-cost AND live-realistic (R10) numbers exist -- a policy choice, not a measured kill (the measured net Sharpe's own 95% CI, 1.148 +/- ~0.96, does not include zero).
expected_ranges.note: Window-specific reference only, NOT an expectation for other windows. Certified replication (Amendment 13, crypto_evidence_v1, 2020-03-16 to 2026-10-03, 6.549 years): gross Sharpe 1.185919, CAGR 54.6399%, vol 45.5044%, max drawdown -51.1439%; net (certification_flat_10bps_per_side) Sharpe 1.148372, CAGR 52.0604%, vol 45.5415%, max drawdown -52.5528%. 50/50 BTC/ETH buy-and-hold over the same window (measured 2026-10-09 directly from the pinned primary CSVs, massive_btcusd_daily.csv / massive_ethusd_daily.csv, no rebalancing -- matching the platform's own independent-sub-account convention): final equity 20.44x, max drawdown -77.60%. The 2016-2020 figures from the legacy, non-evidence fixture (Sharpe 2.10, CAGR 218%) must not appear on any customer-facing surface (R23(e)) and are not repeated here.

expected_ranges.source: No band, deliberately (see expected_ranges[0].source). Declared so that gross AND net are both reported (WP9.9 gross_and_net_reported_check); recomputed from the platform's own certified replication of the evidence window on every read.
expected_ranges.note: Window-specific reference only, NOT an expectation for other windows. Certified replication (Amendment 13, crypto_evidence_v1, 2020-03-16 to 2026-10-03, 6.549 years), net of the certification_flat_10bps_per_side accounting cost (not a realised fill cost): Sharpe 1.148372, CAGR 52.0604%, vol 45.5415%, max drawdown -52.5528%. The paired gross figures are in expected_ranges[0].

known_deviations: The platform runs each coin as an independent sub-account, so weights drift from the published fixed 50/50 rather than truly rebalancing daily (cross_asset_rebalance: preferred, not a hard block).

Evidence window is one crypto cycle (2020 COVID crash, 2021 top, 2022 decline, 2023-2026 recovery) -- a single regime sequence, not several independent cycles; this is exactly why no performance band is published (see expected_ranges[0].source).

C4 venue check (data_quality_certificate.json): Kraken-vs-primary comparison only covers the last 720 days of the window (Kraken's own public history limit); no exception above 150bp was found in that sub-window, but the earlier ~5.5 years have no independent third-source venue check, only the Bitstamp arbiter.
failure_regimes: Bull-market dependence: the rule's edge over buy-and-hold can be small in a strong uptrend (certified net Sharpe 1.148 vs a 50/50 buy-and-hold max drawdown of -77.6% that the rule's own -52.55% net drawdown improves on, but both windows share the same underlying bull market).
Deep drawdowns: crypto volatility (45.5% annualised in the certified window) can far exceed a typical drawdown ladder without scaling down.

Sideways or choppy markets where prices repeatedly cross the 100-day average (whipsaw). GENERAL property of moving-average trend rules; 198 signal flips over 6.549 years in the certified window is the measured turnover, not a claim about future whipsaw frequency.

cost_profile.note: Turnover as a multiple of sleeve equity is NOT recorded in the local files. The certified replication (key_metrics.json) counted 198 asset-level signal flips over 6.548939 years (2393 observations at 365.4027 per year), about 30.2 per year across the two coins. The certified net result above uses the certification_flat_10bps_per_side accounting cost (turnover_sum_x_equity 110.4162, cost_sum_x_equity 0.110416), not a measured spread/impact model for any live venue.

verification_note: Rule text, parameters, requirements and rebalance are copied verbatim from library_curation::draft::RuleTemplate::CryptoTrend100d (the platform's own compiled-rule-template menu) rather than retyped, to guarantee zero drift against the compiled weightsim-rules S3 adapter. Backtest window and all performance numbers come from Amendment 13's real, pre-registered evidence fixture (program/tests/fixtures/replication_ladder_crypto_evidence/, PR #213, merged 2026-10-04): real data pulled by the owner (Massive primary, Bitstamp arbiter, Kraken venue check) per the pre-registered window rule (section 3) and data-quality certificate (section 4), verdict PASS on all of C1/C2/C3/C5 (data_quality_certificate.json), T4 mutation-power check passed (all 5 S3 mutants caught by at least one tier, mutant_replays.json: all_mutants_caught=true, mutants_blocking_certification=[]). This fixture was built and fully certified on 2026-10-04 but its own final step -- drafting this entry -- was never done until now (2026-10-09); nothing in program/src referenced the fixture before this file. The one number NOT already sitting in the fixture, the 50/50 BTC/ETH buy-and-hold drawdown over the certified window, was measured today directly from the fixture's own pinned primary CSVs (massive_btcusd_daily.csv / massive_ethusd_daily.csv) rather than invented: -77.60% (no cross-coin rebalancing, matching the platform's own independent-sub-account convention; a daily-rebalanced 50/50 variant gives a close -76.29%, consistent with the council record's unweighted BTC-alone figure of -76.7%). Per Amendment 13 section 7 and council rulings R22/R23, no performance band is published despite the certification passing representativeness (9.8): the council's own stated reason is statistical power (SE ~0.49 on one ~6.5-year window spanning a single crypto cycle), a deliberate policy choice, not a failed check -- see expected_ranges[0].source for the exact reasoning and the measured net Sharpe's own confidence interval. Version 2 (2026-10-17) changes the cited evidence and, as a pre-merge correction of this still-unmerged entry (not a rule change: the rule text, its 100-day SMA, 50% weights, daily EveryBar rebalance and the compiled rule are unchanged), writes `instruments` and `parameters` exactly as the compiled rule declares them (BTC, ETH; sma_days, weight_per_instrument, schedule, rebalance_policy) so that check A4 finds no RULE_DRIFT, and declares the certified net Sharpe as a second, unbounded sharpe_net range beside sharpe_gross so that check A9 finds both reported. Requirements, rebalance and backtest window are those of version 1. The Liu & Tsyvinski (2021) citation was checked against the actual paper text on 2026-09-23 (reused from this entry's own pre-existing test fixture, program/data/strategy_library/test_fixtures/crypto_trend_100d.json) and honestly disclosed as covering cryptocurrency return predictability generally, including a time-series momentum effect, not this specific 100-day-SMA rule. On 2026-10-17 the three citations in sources were looked up against Crossref (bibliographic record for all three; abstract for the first two; Crossref has no abstract for the third). citation_claims records exactly two hand-authored, abstract-level claims, both short phrases copied from the Crossref abstracts: sources[0] 'there is a strong time-series momentum effect' and sources[2] 'cryptocurrency market, size, and momentum' (cross-sectional momentum; adjacent, not this rule). No numeric claim is made from any paper, and none of the papers' Sharpe ratios is claimed or relied on. The automated generate_library_citation_check fetch of the live pages has not been run for version 2 (it needs a network-capable operator run); until it is, these claims are verified by hand at abstract level only. Limitations: the literature supports time-series momentum in crypto as a documented effect over the papers' own samples; it does not validate the 100-day-SMA rule, and the single certified evidence window remains one crypto cycle. CONCRETE CONSEQUENCE of the withheld performance band: replication::admission::admission_for's 9.7_evidence_strength check requires a PerformanceBand range with a real low bound, which this entry does not have -- this entry is therefore served on GET /api/library (real, visible data) but is Held, not Admitted, and proposals.rs rejects any mandate's attempt to actually propose it with that exact reason until a performance band with a real low bound exists for it. Version 2 does not change that: it hand-sets no band.
retirement_rule: Flag to the inbox for a human decision (the agent may not remove it on its own) when any of: (a) the monthly fidelity check finds signal agreement with the compiled reference implementation below 0.98; (b) the sleeve's own replayed drawdown reaches the mandate's first drawdown rung; (c) realised net results over a full evaluation window fall outside a performance band once one is published; (d) a later decay_check replication run against this same rule_hash fails. The window length and any numeric tolerance for (c) must be set by the owner before go-live; none is assumed here.
